parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 # ParallelDocs — a side-by-side documentation ecosystem
 
 Have you ever wished a “side track” for code the way DVD extras let filmmakers talk over a film **without** changing the picture? When looking at code, that might answer the whys, reveal the intent **besides** the code itself.
 
 The **ecosystem** is a few published **`@parallel-docs/*` libraries** (shared config and paths, Markdown → HTML, static “code + parallel-docs” pages), the **`parallel-docs` CLI**, and a **VS Code / Cursor** extension—all agreeing on **`.parallel-docs.toml`** and the **`.parallel-docs/`** tree. **Tooling** keeps companions tied to the source: optional **Git pre-commit**, **`validate`** / **`doctor`**, migrations, **`render`** / **`pages:build`** / **`serve`** for browsable HTML, and **[standalone binaries](https://github.com/d-led/parallel-docs/releases)** for machines without Node. This repo’s own CI runs the **quality gate** (format, lint, typecheck, unit tests, etc.) and **Cypress** against a built static site—it does **not** run `parallel-docs validate` as a separate step unless you add that to your workflow.

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 ## Why
 
 Inline comments are not always possible (generated files, tight formats, policy). ParallelDocs keeps the primary artifact clean while storing rationale, warnings, and diagrams in **parallel-docs**—Markdown that lives under `.parallel-docs/source/` beside the code it explains. In a meeting you might hear: _“We have to document our architecture **in parallel-docs** so that newcomers can have an effective source code onboarding experience.”_ Same word names the tool and the practice; context disambiguates.
 
 The same split is useful when you want **rich context for a human or a chatbot**—runbooks, product rationale, incident notes, onboarding prose—that does not belong in the source file itself, yet stays **correlatable** with specific lines or regions through the metadata index and block anchors, so the assistant can reason about “this parallel-docs goes with that code” without you pasting a wall of inline comments into the repo.
 
 **Good for:** **developers**, **architects**, and **LLM**-assisted workflows that each need **context-specific** insight into the same codebase with different rationale, warnings, and diagrams beside the source without crowding the primary file. Also onboarding next to the code, pre-commit validation of companion metadata, and publishing a **code + parallel-docs** static site (for example GitHub Pages) with scroll-linked panes.

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 ## Using ParallelDocs
 
 Short, command-first guides (install the CLI or extension, first `.parallel-docs/` setup, validation, and what each layer catches):
 
 - [Install](docs/user/install.md) — binaries, `npm i -g parallel-docs` / `npx parallel-docs` (`--help` → `Usage: parallel-docs [options] [command]`), editor extension
 - [Quickstart](docs/user/quickstart.md) — `parallel-docs init`, paired Markdown paths, validate
 - [Keeping blocks in sync](docs/user/keeping-blocks-in-sync.md) — index, markers, anchors
 - [What ParallelDocs detects](docs/user/detection.md) — hook, CLI, editor, known gaps
 - [CLI reference](docs/user/cli.md) — commands, exit codes, env vars
 - [Configuration](docs/user/config.md) — `.parallel-docs.toml` keys
 - [Troubleshooting](docs/user/troubleshooting.md) — common failures

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 ## Dogfood: narrow Pages + scroll-linked flip
 
 On [GitHub Pages](https://d-led.github.io/parallel-docs/), use a **narrow** viewport (or a phone), **scroll this README to the bottom**, then use **flip source / parallel-docs**. Scroll should stay **block-linked** with this companion file, and a **second flip control** appears when the toolbar flip scrolls off-screen.

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 [render]
 mermaid = true
 syntaxTheme = "github-dark"
 relative_github_blob_links = true

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 [static_site]
 title = "ParallelDocs"
 github_url = "https://github.com/d-led/parallel-docs"
 # Optional source-link base when _site/ doesn't host repo files:
 # source_link_prefix = "https://github.com/d-led/parallel-docs/blob/main"
 default_source_file = "README.md"
 default_angle = "main"
 github_blob_branch = "main"

parallel-docs-snippet/v1
 [angles]
 default_angle = "main"
 
 [[angles.definitions]]
 id = "main"
 title = "Main"
 
 [[angles.definitions]]
 id = "architecture"
 title = "Architecture"
